questions.question: Explain the major food and nutritional requirements of adults. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the major food and nutritional requirements of adults. [An] / [CO2]
  • Energy needs should match age, sex, body size and physical activity to maintain healthy body weight.
  • Include cereals/millets or other whole grains, pulses, vegetables, fru its, and suitable protein foods.
  • Provide adequate high-quality protein for maintenance and tissue repair. Ensure adequate vitamins and
  • minerals, especially calcium, iron and other nutrients according to individual needs. Include healthy fats,
  • dietary fibre and sufficient water; limit excess salt, added sugar and saturated/trans fats.
  • Scheme: 1 mark for each of the five key points.

questions.question: Explain the importance of nutrition during adolescent growth. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of nutrition during adolescent growth. [K] / [CO5]
  • Adolescence involves rapid increases in height, weight and tissue development, increasing energy needs.
  • Protein supports growth and repair of body tissues. Calcium and vitamin D support bone growth and
  • peak bone mass. Iron needs rise, particularly after menstruation begins; iron -rich foods help prevent
  • deficiency. A varied balanced diet, supports learning, immunity and physical activity; limit nutrient-poor
  • foods.
  • Scheme: 1 mark for each of the five key points.

questions.question: Describe the role of prolactin in lactation. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of prolactin in lactation. [U] / [CO3]
  • Prolactin is a hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. During pregnancy, prolactin levels rise
  • and prepare the mammary glands for milk production. After delivery, the fall in oes trogen and
  • progesterone permits prolactin to support milk synthesis. Suckling stimulates prolactin release, helping
  • maintain milk production. Frequent and effective breastfeeding supports continued production; prolactin
  • produces milk.
  • Scheme: 1 mark for each of the five key points.

questions.question: Describe the role and functions of the placenta during pregnancy. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role and functions of the placenta during pregnancy. [U] / [CO3]
  • The placenta is a temporary organ that develops in the uterus and connects the foetus to the mother
  • through the umbilical cord. (2 marks).
  • Transfers oxygen and nutrients from maternal to foetal circulation. Transfers carbon dioxide and
  • metabolic waste products from the foetus for removal by the maternal organs. Acts as an endocrine
  • organ, producing hormones such as hCG, progesterone, oestrogens and human placental lactog en to
  • support pregnancy. Provides selective protection and transfers maternal IgG antibodies, contributing to
  • passive immunity; it is not a complete barrier to pathogens or harmful substances. Anchors the
  • developing pregnancy through its attachment to the uterine wall and supports exchange between
  • maternal and foetal blood without normally mixing them directly.
  • Scheme: Definition : 2 marks, Role and function – 2 marks each (Any 4)

questions.question: Discuss the protective and immunological factors present in human milk. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the protective and immunological factors present in human milk. [U] / [CO4]
  • • Secretory IgA provides mucosal protection by helping prevent pat hogens from attaching to and
  • entering the infant’s tissues.
  • Lactoferrin binds iron and can inhibit the growth of some harmful bacteria.
  • • Lysozyme damages bacterial cell walls and contributes to antimicrobial protection.
  • • Human milk oligosaccharides act as prebiotics and can prevent some pathogens from attaching to the
  • intestinal lining.
  • • Leukocytes and other immune components, including cytokines and protective proteins, contribute to
  • immune defence.
  • • These factors support development of the infant gu t microbiota and reduce the risk or severity of some
  • infections, especially gastrointestinal infections.
  • • Colostrum is particularly concentrated in immune factors; human milk provides ongoing protection but
  • does not eliminate all infection risk.
  • Scheme: Any 5 factors – 2 marks each
